title: Summer growth spurt

clues.t: I grow by several centimetres on a hot summer's day.
I was only meant to stand for 20 years, but I turned out to be a handy radio mast.
Leading artists signed a furious protest against me before I was even finished.
I was the star of the 1889 World's Fair.
I get repainted about every seven years, by hand, in my own shade of brown.
330 metres of iron lattice, towering over the River Seine in Paris.

pearl: My engineer kept a small private apartment near my summit, and entertained guests including Thomas Edison there.

title: Hill with a secret

clues.t: The world's largest pyramid by volume is mine, and it isn't in Egypt.
My capital is slowly sinking, because it was built on an old lake bed.
I gave the world chocolate, chillies and vanilla.
Millions of monarch butterflies fly thousands of kilometres to spend winter in my forests.
Every year families honour their dead with marigolds and painted sugar skulls.
Mariachi bands, tacos and tequila.

pearl: The Great Pyramid of Cholula is so overgrown it looks like a natural hill, with a church sitting on top.

title: Point taken

clues.t: I grew out of a military code meant for reading messages silently in the dark.
My inventor was just 15 when he worked out my first version.
He lost his sight in childhood after an accident in his father's harness workshop.
Each of my cells has six positions, enough for 64 different patterns.
You'll find me on lift buttons and medicine boxes.
A French teenager's system of raised dots, read with the fingertips.

pearl: World Braille Day falls on 4 January, my inventor's birthday, and France moved his remains to the Panthéon in 1952.

title: Big cat energy

clues.t: My working title was 'King of the Jungle', which was awkward, given there's no jungle in me.
Animators studied real big cats brought into the studio.
My stage version is the highest-earning show in Broadway history.
Elton John won an Oscar for one of my songs.
A scheming uncle, a stampede in a gorge, and a young hero who runs away from home.
'Hakuna Matata', Simba, and a baby held up on Pride Rock.

pearl: Simba really is Swahili for 'lion', and 'hakuna matata' really is a Swahili phrase. It means 'no worries'.

title: Never lost a passenger

clues.t: A heavy weight thrown at someone else hit my head when I was a teenager, and left me with sudden sleeping spells for life.
I was born with the name Araminta Ross.
In the American Civil War I volunteered as a nurse, a cook, a scout and a spy.
I helped guide the Combahee River Raid, which freed more than 700 people.
I made about 13 dangerous trips back into the American South, leading about 70 people to freedom.
The most famous 'conductor' on the Underground Railroad, nicknamed Moses.

pearl: Late in life she said: 'I never ran my train off the track, and I never lost a passenger.'

title: Acquired taste

clues.t: My tingling kick comes from ammonium chloride, which was also a classic cough-medicine ingredient.
My name traces back to Latin for 'salt of Ammon', after an ancient Egyptian temple site.
In the Nordic countries you'll find me in ice cream, chocolate and even vodka.
I'm usually sold as small black diamonds.
Visitors try me once, pull a face and ask what they did wrong.
Finland's beloved salty liquorice.

pearl: Finns mix me into a vodka-based drink nicknamed 'Salmari'. Happy Independence Day, Finland.

title: Frequent flyer

clues.t: My shoulder can lock in place, so I can glide for hours almost without flapping.
After leaving the nest, I can spend years at sea without touching land.
A poem warned sailors that killing me would bring terrible luck.
My wingspan can reach about 3.5 metres, the longest of any living bird.
I soar over the Southern Ocean and pair up with one partner for life.
A huge seabird, and also what golfers call three under par.

pearl: A Laysan albatross called Wisdom was still hatching chicks on Midway Atoll in her seventies.

title: Not visible from space

clues.t: Legend says astronauts can spot me from space. They mostly can't.
Sticky rice was mixed into the mortar for some of my stonework.
I'm not one structure at all, but many built over about 2,000 years.
The Ming dynasty gave my most famous sections their brick and watchtowers.
A 2012 survey measured my total length at more than 21,000 kilometres.
Tourists hike me just north of Beijing. I was built to keep out invaders.

pearl: That 2012 measurement, 21,196 km, is more than half way around the equator.

title: Spin-off island

clues.t: I split away from India about 88 million years ago.
About 90% of my wildlife lives nowhere else on Earth.
Early settlers sailed from Borneo, so my language is a cousin of Malay.
I'm the world's biggest producer of vanilla.
Tourists come to photograph my Avenue of the Baobabs.
Lemurs, the world's fourth-largest island, and a very silly DreamWorks cartoon.

pearl: I was once home to elephant birds, which laid the largest eggs known from any land animal, bigger than any dinosaur's.

title: Explosive idea

clues.t: I get my name from the Greek word for 'power'.
My secret ingredient is a soft, crumbly earth that soaks up an unstable liquid.
I was patented in 1867.
My inventor's younger brother died in a laboratory blast three years before.
My inventor left his fortune to fund the world's most famous prizes.
Red sticks with a fuse, in every old cartoon.

pearl: Alfred Nobel died on 10 December 1896, which is why the prizes are handed out on this day every year.

title: Over the hills

clues.t: The real family I'm based on left by train, not on foot over the mountains.
The real father was a decorated submarine commander.
I'm drawn from a real Austrian woman's 1949 memoir.
I won five Oscars, including Best Picture for 1965.
A nun who keeps getting in trouble leaves the abbey to look after seven children.
Do-Re-Mi, Edelweiss and hills alive in Salzburg.

pearl: The mountains above Salzburg lead to Germany, not Switzerland, so the film's final walk heads in a rather unhelpful direction.

title: Rose diagram

clues.t: I drew a famous wedge-shaped 'rose' chart to show in numbers why soldiers were dying.
I was the first woman elected to the Royal Statistical Society.
My parents named me after the Italian city where I was born.
I had a pet owl called Athena that rode in my pocket.
I made my name at the Scutari military hospital in the Crimean War.
The Lady with the Lamp, founder of modern nursing.

pearl: International Nurses Day is held on her birthday, 12 May.

title: Short and sharp

clues.t: A Turin inventor patented a steam machine to brew me in bulk in 1884.
A 1948 lever machine from Milan's Achille Gaggia gave me my famous foam, the crema.
I'm made by forcing hot water through finely ground beans at about nine bars of pressure.
I take just 25 to 30 seconds to make.
I'm served in a tiny cup, often standing up at the bar.
The Italian shot of coffee underneath every latte and cappuccino.

pearl: In Italy, ordering a 'latte' gets you a glass of plain milk. A jump-start of a different kind.

title: Hello, sucker

clues.t: I have three jaws and leave a Y-shaped bite.
My spit keeps blood flowing, so dinner doesn't stop early.
My body has 32 segments, each with its own little nerve centre.
People kept me in fancy jars and used me for centuries in bloodletting.
I have 10 eyes and can drink several times my own weight in one meal.
A slimy bloodsucking worm that latches onto hikers' ankles.

pearl: After a big meal I can go months, even up to a year, before I need to eat again.

title: Thumbs down

clues.t: My name probably came from a giant statue of an emperor that stood nearby.
Sailors once hauled a huge awning over me to shade the crowds.
Ancient writers claim I was flooded for mock sea battles.
Earthquakes and stone-robbers took about two-thirds of me.
I opened in AD 80 and could seat about 50,000 spectators.
Rome's great arena, famous for gladiators.

pearl: The Roman historian Cassius Dio says the opening games lasted 100 days.

title: Ode to joy

clues.t: My bakers claim more than 3,000 kinds of bread.
One of my dukes passed a beer purity law in 1516.
Stretches of my motorways have no official speed limit.
Gutenberg's printing press was born here, in Mainz.
Bonn, once my western capital, is where Beethoven was born.
Berlin, Oktoberfest and bratwurst.

pearl: Beethoven was baptised on 17 December 1770, so today's date is only a best guess at his birthday.

title: Colour-blind name

clues.t: I was dreamed up in 1954 by a chemist in Melbourne.
Officials at first showed little interest in him. One pilot group feared I'd spy on them.
Mystery crashes of the first passenger jets, the Comets, inspired me.
I have to survive fire, impact and deep water, and I ping to help people find me.
I record the instruments and what was said in the cockpit.
After a plane crash, investigators hunt for me, even though I'm bright orange.

pearl: David Warren's idea caught on in Britain first, and in 1967 Australia became the first country to require both data and voice recorders.

title: Please look after this

clues.t: My creator got the idea from a lone teddy on a shop shelf on Christmas Eve 1956.
He also remembered wartime evacuee children with labels round their necks.
My 2014 big-screen outing had a taxidermist villain played by Nicole Kidman.
I stow away on a ship from darkest Peru to London.
A kind family finds me at the railway station I'm named after.
A duffle coat, a red hat and marmalade sandwiches.

pearl: Michael Bond's bear was originally from Africa, until his agent pointed out there are no bears there.

title: Honk if you love Christmas

clues.t: Domestic ones of my kind can live for more than 20 years.
Roman legend says my ancestors saved the city by honking when invaders crept up at night.
On the ground, a group of us is a gaggle. In the air, it’s a skein.
We fly in a V shape, which saves energy for the birds behind.
In a famous fairy tale, one of us lays golden eggs.
Bob Cratchit’s family ate one of me for Christmas, before Scrooge sent round the prize turkey.

pearl: Before turkeys took over, goose was the classic English Christmas dinner. Victorian families often saved up through a ‘goose club’ to afford one.

title: Dig deep

clues.t: Korean scientists spent years making a special space-friendly version of me for their first astronaut.
People have special fridges just for me.
My communal winter-making tradition, kimjang, is on UNESCO's heritage list.
I wasn't always red. Chilli only arrived a few hundred years ago.
I was traditionally stored in clay pots buried in the ground.
Spicy fermented cabbage, Korea's national side dish.

pearl: Koreans often say my name instead of 'cheese' when posing for a photo.

title: Slow and steady

clues.t: One of my kind on the island of St Helena is thought to have hatched around 1832.
Sailors stacked me live in ships' holds, because I could survive for months without food or water.
Charles Darwin rode on my back, and wrote that he found it hard to stay on.
A group of Pacific islands is named after a Spanish word for me.
I can weigh more than 250 kg and my pace is famously relaxed.
I wear a huge domed shell, and my smaller cousin once beat a hare in a race.

pearl: Jonathan, the giant tortoise on St Helena, is the oldest known living land animal. He takes life very slowly. It seems to work.

title: Grief in marble

clues.t: My four minarets lean slightly outward, said to be so they'd fall away from the tomb in an earthquake.
Flowers of precious stone are inlaid into my walls.
Pollution has yellowed me, so workers clean me with mud packs.
About 20,000 workers built me over two decades in the 1600s.
A heartbroken Mughal emperor built me for his wife, Mumtaz.
India's famous white marble tomb, in Agra.

pearl: I'm famously, almost mathematically symmetrical. The only thing out of place is the emperor's own tomb, squeezed in beside hers.

title: First to the ballot

clues.t: In 1893 I became the first self-governing country where women could vote.
One of my hills has an 85-letter name.
I have roughly five sheep for every person.
My Māori name is often translated as 'land of the long white cloud'.
I'm where Hobbiton was filmed.
Kiwis, the All Blacks and the haka.

pearl: Suffragist Kate Sheppard led the campaign and now appears on the country's ten-dollar note.

title: Pull!

clues.t: My inventor was a London sweet-maker in the 1840s.
He got the idea from French sugared almonds, twisted up in tissue paper.
Legend says the bang came to him while listening to a crackling log fire.
I first held a love motto. Sweets and toys came later.
My inventor's son added the paper hat.
Two people pull me at Christmas dinner, then groan at the joke inside.

pearl: Love mottoes came first. The terrible jokes only moved in decades later.

title: Family holiday

clues.t: Many of my sets were built inside a closed-down high school.
The gangster film my star watches was made up and shot just for me.
My music was by John Williams, and it got an Oscar nomination.
An actor agreed to one take with a real tarantula on his face.
A huge family flies to Paris for Christmas and leaves someone behind.
Kevin, two burglars, paint cans on strings and a scream with aftershave.

pearl: Those swinging paint cans are pure physics, so Isaac Newton, born on Christmas Day 1642, would surely approve.

title: Time on your hands

clues.t: Before about 1900, many men thought I was a ladies’ accessory.
Soldiers in World War I made me popular, because fumbling for a pocket version mid-battle was no good.
Some versions of me count your steps and check your heart rate.
Switzerland and Japan are famous for making me.
In the 1920s my face was painted with glowing paint so you could read me in the dark.
The women who painted me got very sick. They became known as the Radium Girls.

pearl: Radium paint on watch dials was replaced by safer glowing materials, and today most use non-radioactive paints that soak up light and release it slowly.

title: Who made me first?

clues.t: Two neighbouring countries still argue over which one made me first.
I'm named after a dancer who toured both of them in 1926.
Vinegar and cornflour give me my soft, marshmallow-like middle.
I'm crisp on the outside and tend to crack. That's fine.
I'm a classic summer Christmas dessert in the Southern Hemisphere.
Meringue, whipped cream, kiwifruit and passionfruit.

pearl: The Oxford English Dictionary's earliest citation for me is a 1927 New Zealand recipe book. Australia has not conceded.

title: With great power

clues.t: Weight for weight, what I make is stronger than steel.
My babies can drift hundreds of kilometres through the air on a thread.
I usually have eight eyes.
I'm an arachnid, not an insect, thanks.
Stan Lee said watching a fly on a wall helped inspire a superhero named after me.
Eight legs and a sticky web in the corner of your bathroom.

pearl: Spider-Man first swung into a comic in 1962. Publisher's verdict: people hate spiders. Readers disagreed.

title: Sails on the harbour

clues.t: My Danish architect quit in 1966 and never saw me finished.
I ran about 1,400% over budget.
A judge is said to have rescued my design from the rejected pile.
My roof wears more than a million cream-and-white Swedish tiles that clean themselves in the rain.
Queen Elizabeth II opened me in 1973.
White sails on Bennelong Point, next to the Harbour Bridge.

pearl: Jørn Utzon won architecture's top award, the Pritzker Prize, in 2003, yet he never returned to see me finished.

title: Fore!

clues.t: My national animal is the unicorn.
I gave the world television's John Logie Baird and penicillin's Alexander Fleming.
An underwater monster is said to live in one of my lochs.
The Old Course at St Andrews makes me the home of golf.
Haggis, bagpipes and a whole lot of tartan.
Edinburgh is my capital, and my neighbour to the south is England.

pearl: My parliament banned golf in 1457, because it was distracting people from archery practice.

title: Bang on time

clues.t: My ancestors were bamboo stalks that popped when thrown on a fire.
Chinese alchemists seeking the secret of eternal life stumbled on my key ingredient.
Strontium makes me red, barium makes me green and copper makes me blue.
Blue is the hardest of my colours to get right.
Handel wrote music for a royal display of me in 1749.
Sydney Harbour, Times Square, midnight, New Year's Eve.

pearl: That royal 1749 display in London set a pavilion on fire. The music went down much better.
